acs.text: Given the text `[a](https://example.com)`, when `markdown.markdown(text, extensions=['external_links'])` is called, then no exception is raised.

Given an instance `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['external_links'])`, when `convert('text')` is called, then the result is `

text

`.

Given the text `[a](https://example.com)`, when `markdown.markdown(text)` is called, then the result is `

a

`.
Given the text `<https://example.com>`, when `markdown.markdown(text)` is called with no extensions, then the result contains neither `target=` nor `rel=`.

Given the text `[a](https://example.com)` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the output contains one `<a` start tag whose attributes include `href="https://example.com"`, `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
Given the text `[a](http://example.com/x?y=1)` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the `<a` start tag includes `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
Given the text `[a](https://example.com)` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the link text and `href` are unchanged: the output contains `href="https://example.com"` and `>a`.
Given the text `<https://example.com>` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the `<a` start tag includes `href="https://example.com"`, `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
Given the text `<mailto:a@example.com>` or `<a@example.com>` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the output contains neither `target=` nor `rel=`.

Given the text `[a][1]` followed by a blank line and `[1]: https://example.com`, with the extension enabled, when converted, then the `<a` start tag includes `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

Given the text `[a](/docs/page.html)` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the result is `

a

`.

Given the text `[a](#section)` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the result is `

a

`.
Given the text `[a](mailto:a@example.com)` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the output contains neither `target=` nor `rel=`.

Given the text `[a](page.html)` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the result is `

a

`.

Given the text `![alt](https://example.com/i.png)` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the result is `

`.

Given the text `[![alt](https://example.com/i.png)](https://example.com)` and the extension enabled, when converted, then the `<a` start tag includes `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and the `<img` tag contains neither `target=` nor `rel=`.

Given the extension named `external_links`, when `markdown.markdown('[a](https://example.com)', extensions=['external_links'])` is called, then no configuration is needed and the output matches AC-FR-003-1.

questions.title: Raw HTML anchors
questions.question: Does decision 3 cover `<a>` elements written as raw HTML in the Markdown source?
questions.options: (a) Yes, add the attributes (b) No, leave raw HTML unchanged (c) Other

questions.title: Existing target or rel values
questions.question: When an external link already has `target` or `rel`, are they kept, replaced, or merged?
questions.options: (a) Keep the existing values (b) Replace with `_blank` and `noopener noreferrer` (c) Merge `rel` tokens, keep `target` (d) Other

questions.title: Scheme case and protocol-relative links
questions.question: Are `HTTPS://example.com` and `//example.com` external?
questions.options: (a) Only the two lowercase prefixes (b) Case-insensitive scheme (c) Also `//host` (d) Other
